a: softmax(z)_i = e^(z_i) / Σ_j e^(z_j) turns logits into a probability distribution.
ReLU(x) = max(0, x) is a common neural network activation.
Cross-entropy measures the difference between true labels and predicted probabilities.
Gradient descent updates parameters opposite the gradient to minimize a loss.
Learning rate is the step size in optimization; too large diverges, too small is slow.
cosine(a,b) = (a·b) / (|a||b|) measures angle similarity of vectors.
Normalization often scales to [0,1]; standardization centers mean 0 and scales by std dev.
log2(n) is common in CS for binary splits and complexity (e.g. binary search).
AND &, OR |, XOR ^, NOT ~, shifts << >> operate on binary representations.
a % n is the remainder after dividing a by n (language-specific for negatives).
Floating point approximates reals with finite precision; expect rounding error.
Numerically stable algorithms avoid catastrophic cancellation and overflow/underflow.
Interpolation estimates values between known data points.
Linear regression fits a line (or hyperplane) minimizing squared error to predict continuous targets.
